J.P. Morgan says SKF auto spin-off no longer weighs on shares
sum: Investing.com — J.P. Morgan в пятницу повысил рейтинг акций SKF, акции которой котируются в Швеции, с «недостаточного» до «нейтрального», заявив, что запланированное выделение ее автомобильного бизнеса больше не является бременем для акций.
Брокер повысил целевую цену на декабрь 2027 года с 250 крон до 300 крон. 12 ноября акции SKF стоили 282 кроны и в этом году выросли на 14,7%.

Базовый сценарий J.P. Morgan предполагает потенциал роста на 6% от этой цены, при этом оставшийся бизнес SKF оценивается в 11,5 раз больше прогнозируемой операционной прибыли на 2027 год, а автомобильное подразделение Vertevo — в семь раз.

Оценка оставшегося бизнеса в 10 раз по «медвежьему» сценарию предполагает цену акций в 258 крон, или потенциал падения на 9%, тогда как 13-кратная оценка по бычьему сценарию предполагает 342 кроны, или потенциал роста на 21%. Текущая цена акций предполагает увеличение стоимости оставшегося бизнеса в 11 раз.
В рамках выделения акционеры получат одну акцию SKF Vertevo B за каждые пять принадлежащих им акций SKF B.
Исходная дата — 26 ноября, а акции Vertevo B должны начать торговаться на Nasdaq Stockholm 1 декабря. 17 ноября Vertevo проводит день рынков капитала.
Ожидается, что выделение приведет к изменению индекса. MSCI удалит Vertevo из своих стандартных индексов и добавит его в индексы компаний малой капитализации при закрытии 1 декабря.

Nissan cuts sales outlook again but keeps profit target
sum: Nissan cut its full-year global sales forecast for the second time since August on Wednesday, blaming China, while keeping its profit and cash targets because its Chinese business sits outside its consolidated operating profit.

The Japanese carmaker now expects retail sales of 2.97 million to 3 million vehicles in the year ending March 2027, down from 3.15 million, which was itself reduced from 3.3 million in August. It maintained guidance of 13 trillion yen in revenue, 200 billion yen in operating profit and 20 billion yen in net income.

Second-quarter operating profit fell 96 per cent to 2.1 billion yen, far below the 54.9 billion yen analysts expected, according to FactSet figures cited by CNBC. Net revenue rose 8.2 per cent to 3.1 trillion yen. Chief Financial Officer George Leondis told analysts that roughly 30 billion yen of specific factors, split about evenly between lost production after the Kumamoto earthquake, the timing of cost reductions and tax settlements, had depressed the quarter.

The half-year picture is better. Operating profit was 80 billion yen, an improvement of 108 billion yen year on year, on a 1.3 per cent margin, and the net loss narrowed to 39.7 billion yen from 222 billion yen.

Leondis gave the mechanism directly: China is equity accounted, so its results fall below the operating profit line. Nissan cut its China volume outlook and raised its forecasts for the Americas and Japan. Management also expects the usual second-half weighting, historically 53 to 55 per cent of annual sales.

Chief Executive Ivan Espinosa said industry volume in China fell 22 per cent in the first half while Nissan's retail sales fell 15 per cent, with the decline widening to 31.5 per cent across the first nine months of the calendar year. Nissan cut Chinese production by 16.3 per cent. Espinosa said the brand is still recognised there for lower-priced petrol cars, notably the Sylphy, while buyers shift to new energy vehicles faster than expected.

Espinosa told CNBC the company would expand exports of China-developed vehicles from two models and two markets to five models and 12 country clusters. "We can defend ourselves from these very aggressive players by using exactly the same elements that they have: speed, cost, and good technology," he said.

Polestar Unveils Formula 2030 Concept as US Sales Door Closes in 2027
sum: Polestar has pulled the wraps off a low-slung, four-door electric sports concept called the Formula 2030, a styling exercise that previews the design language of its next-generation models — even though the brand will be barred from selling new cars in the United States beginning in 2027.

The Swedish automaker, which is majority-owned by China's Geely, unveiled the concept on Tuesday. It measures 184 inches long and stands just 53 inches tall, roughly the footprint of a Polestar 2 but with a far lower roofline. Polestar places the car in its own segment between the successor to the Polestar 2, due in 2027, and the Polestar 7 SUV, expected in 2028.

The US restriction stems from the Connected Vehicle Rule, which limits sales of cars containing software or hardware sourced from China or Russia. Automakers can seek authorization to keep selling; Volvo, which shares the same parent as Polestar, obtained one, while Polestar has not. The Bureau of Industry and Security's ban takes effect in 2027.

The concept's front end is described as a preview of the next Polestar 2, while its rear light signature — a departure from the full-width bars common on EVs — will appear on future production cars. "We wanted to evolve, while respecting, the core design values we demonstrated with previous models that define the Polestar brand in such a recognizable way," said Nahum Escobedo, Polestar's head of exterior design. He said the team pushed "perceptions, preconceptions, and the expected" through its choices in form language and new detailing, including the Single Blade rear lights.

Inside, the Formula 2030 leans further into minimalism than prior Polestars but adds something the brand has not offered before: physical controls. Rocker switches and rotary controllers sit below a 12.2-inch center screen, paired with a 20-inch curved driver display mounted on the steering column and a user-configurable interface. Four individual seats use inflatable bolsters that adjust to the occupant, with seat backs made from European flax and bio-based polypropylene. Voice control runs on Google Gemini. A concealed LiDAR sensor deploys only when the car enters autonomous mode.

BlackBerry Is Up 136% This Year: Take Profits, or Buy More?
sum: This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Few software turnarounds have paid off in 2026 like BlackBerry (NYSE:BB), as its QNX embedded operating system keeps winning over automakers. BlackBerry stock is at $8.94, up 2% in afternoon trading; that gain adds to a 136% climb year to date (YTD).

QNX now carries most of the BlackBerry story. The real-time software runs safety-critical systems in cars, robots and industrial machines, alongside a Secure Communications unit that serves governments. That mix sets the company apart from automotive software peers that have struggled this year. Even so, the long-term chart tempers the excitement, since BlackBerry stock still trades below its level of five years ago.

BlackBerry’s biggest catalyst arrived on September 24, when the company reported Q2 FY2027 results that beat expectations on both lines. The company’s revenue rose 26% year over year (YoY) to $163.3 million, ahead of the $145.5 million consensus, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.07 exceeded the $0.04 estimate. Record QNX revenue reached $80.3 million, up 27%, with an 87% adjusted gross margin. Management also raised its FY2027 revenue outlook to $616 million to $636 million.

Licensing revenue at BlackBerry hit $22.1 million, lifted mostly by a new licensing arrangement that management said shouldn’t be viewed as a new quarterly run rate. Setting that one-time boost aside, QNX still drove the quarter, which included the largest design win in QNX history. Coretura, the commercial truck joint venture of Volvo Group and Daimler Truck, picked the QNX-based Alloy Kore platform, adding more than $100 million to the royalty backlog.

A design win means a customer has chosen a supplier’s technology for a future vehicle program. Royalties follow only as those vehicles ship, often years later, which is why BlackBerry management noted the Coretura deal won’t materially change revenue this fiscal year.
A smart front-camera platform from BlackBerry’s QNX unit and Valeo had secured design wins with multiple automakers in China as of November 8, with production expected this year.

XPeng's Research Lab, Korean Showroom and Robotaxi Fleet All Face the Same November 16 Reckoning
sum: XPeng shares climbed 7.2% on Friday, carried by a broader recovery in Chinese electric-vehicle and growth stocks after the sell-off that followed the US midterm elections. No company-specific catalyst drove the move that day, according to media reports. The gain came instead from a sector-wide shift in sentiment — and it lands just as investors are weighing whether XPeng's operational momentum can survive contact with its own financial statements.
That test arrives on November 16, 2026, when the company releases unaudited third-quarter results before US markets open.

The most recent piece of XPeng news was technological rather than commercial. On Wednesday the company, working with Peking University, the University of Hong Kong and other academic partners, unveiled GroundingPI — an open-source foundation model for visual perception aimed at the field of physical AI.

In its research team's evaluation, GroundingPI averaged 73.68 across 34 perception benchmarks. XPeng was explicit that the work is exploratory. No integration into commercial products was announced alongside the publication, and the company said the research does not demonstrate commercial readiness. For investors, the model is a signal of ambition rather than a revenue line; its practical value would only be proven by later real-world use.

Expansion is where the operational scorecard gets more concrete. On Tuesday, Asia Business Daily reported that XPeng Motors Korea has appointed Lee Mansik, formerly of Volvo Cars Korea, to lead the Korean business from December 1. A named executive gives the market-entry plan a clear point of accountability, though the real measure will be how convincingly XPeng converts the announced launch into customers.

The base for that push is stronger than it was a year ago. October deliveries hit a record 50,237 vehicles, up 22% month on month and 20% year on year. Overseas shipments also set a monthly record, climbing 166% year on year to 13,326 units — a figure that gives the international strategy real weight, provided XPeng can keep building on it.
A second gauge of execution sits in Guangzhou.

Ikea sales slide to €43.8B as inflation pressures global furniture demand
sum: Investing.com -- Inter IKEA Group reported a decline in full-year earnings and system-wide retail sales, reflecting prolonged pressure on household budgets and persistent cost headwinds across the global furnishing sector. Total retail sales across the brand's 13 franchise groups fell to €43.8 billion for the fiscal year ended August, down from €44.6 billion a year earlier, marking a third consecutive year of contraction on a currency-adjusted basis.

The Swedish furniture giant saw its operating profit drop roughly 15% to €1.46 billion as wholesale demand from franchisee partners softened amid cautious consumer spending. Revenue at Inter IKEA, which supplies finished goods to franchise operators, slipped to €25.9 billion from €26.3 billion, while net income retreated to €1.4 billion.

Operational performance faced dual headwinds from subdued consumer demand and localized supply-chain frictions that lifted logistics and commodity expenses. In response to margin compression, the franchisor executed an organizational restructuring that eliminated 850 positions globally to simplify operations and reduce internal fragmentation.

Despite the earnings pressure, the group is doubling down on volume-driven discounting to reignite market momentum and restore top-line growth. Inter IKEA and its European franchise partners jointly deployed roughly €1.2 billion toward customer price cuts starting September 1, absorbing near-term profitability to reinforce the brand's low-cost positioning.

To capture shifting consumer habits, franchise operators continued rolling out small-format city locations and opened the brand's first retail store in New Zealand alongside dedicated digital platforms. At the same time, the chain optimized its brick-and-mortar footprint through selective store closures in underperforming markets to maintain capital discipline.

Management maintained that lower retail prices remain the primary catalyst required to reverse volume declines in an uncertain macroeconomic environment. "To reach more people with affordable home furnishing, we need to return to growth," Chief Executive Jakub Jankowski noted, signaling that price investments and operational efficiency will remain central to the group's forward strategy.

OMXS30 closes at 3,301.09 after late-session reversal
sum: The OMXS30 ended Thursday's session at 3,301.09, down 0.32% from the previous close of 3,311.67. The close followed a volatile session in Stockholm: Nasdaq's official OMXS30 overview recorded an intraday high of 3,346.58 and a low of 3,322.02, while Placera reported the closing level and the day's reversal.

According to Placera, Swedish shares initially rose as investors assessed the result of the US midterm election. The market then turned lower when Wall Street opened with sharp declines, particularly among technology stocks. The report also noted that Swedish October inflation was lower than expected and that the Bank of England raised interest rates as expected. These developments formed the broader backdrop to a session in which the OMXS30 moved from an early advance to a negative close.

The shift in sentiment was also reflected in broader European trading. A separate Investing.com report said telecoms, oil and gas, and basic materials were among the weaker sectors. About 36.0 billion Swedish kronor in shares changed hands on the Stockholm exchange, according to Placera.

ABB was one of the clearest drags among OMXS30 constituents, falling 4.3% after China indicated that it would not approve SoftBank's acquisition of ABB's robotics division. Placera reported that China accounts for about 30% of the robotics business. Ericsson declined 4.2% after reports that Elon Musk's SpaceX had agreed with Qualcomm to provide technology for a nationwide US 5G network. Saab also fell 4.2%, while Skanska lost 1.4% after reporting an operating profit below the FactSet consensus.

At the other end of the index, Nibe B rose 2.1%, Essity B gained 1.9% and Volvo advanced 1.7%, according to Investing.com. The site also identified ABB, Ericsson and Saab as the weakest performers. The contrasting performance underlined the defensive and company-specific elements of the session, even as the late technology-led sell-off dominated the index direction.
For further coverage of the index, visit the OMXS30 topic page.

sum: Investing.com -- Nobia AB (ST:NOBI) shares punge 19% on Wednesday after the Swedish kitchen maker's adjusted operating profit fell by almost a third and it burned SEK 157 million of cash in the third quarter, while warning that the ramp-up of its new Jönköping plant is still unresolved.
Adjusted operating profit was SEK 47 million, down from SEK 69 million a year earlier, even though adjusted gross margin rose to 37.9% from 36.8%.

Chief Executive Jesper Gylling Olsen said profitability remained under pressure from the Nobia Park ramp-up, unfinished supply chain consolidation and "a cost base designed for a larger and more geographically diverse group than the Nordic-focused business we operate today."
Free cash flow was an outflow of SEK 157 million, compared with an inflow of SEK 12 million a year earlier.

Operating profit was SEK 14 million, versus a loss of SEK 211 million a year earlier. Items affecting comparability were a charge of SEK 33 million, versus SEK 280 million, mainly for moving production in Sweden from Tidaholm to Nobia Park in Jönköping.
The net loss after tax was SEK 53 million, versus a loss of SEK 1.92 billion a year earlier, or SEK 0.35 per share versus SEK 20.30.

Net sales rose to SEK 1.28 billion from SEK 1.26 billion, helped by a positive currency effect. Organic sales fell by less than 1%, versus growth of 1% a year earlier, mainly because of the transformation in Finland.

sum: Its October passenger vehicles sales climb 11% as exports double and local deliveries fall
CHINA’S biggest carmaker BYD reported higher sales for the sixth straight month as exports made up for slumping demand at home.

BYD’s October passenger vehicles sales climbed 11 per cent as exports doubled and local deliveries fell, according to a statement on Sunday (Nov 1). Chery Automobile, the nation’s biggest exporter, reported sales increased 5 per cent, with exports climbing by 60 per cent.
Shares of BYD and Chery rose in Hong Kong trading on Monday as the continued strength of overseas demand for Chinese cars helped ease concerns about the prolonged downturn in their home market.
Still, export growth has not necessarily impressed investors as BYD last week reported earnings and revenue that missed analyst estimates.
Among other automakers, Geely Automobile Holdings’ overseas sales more than doubled, allowing it to squeeze out a 1 per cent gain in total deliveries.
Xiaomi and Xpeng’s monthly sales surpassed 50,000, while Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology delivered more than 100,000 vehicles for a fourth consecutive month.

Polestar barred from US over the Chinese connected vehicle rule, a dangerous precedent
sum: Polestar is pulling new vehicles out of the US market starting with model year 2027 after the Commerce Department declined to grant it authorization under the Connected Vehicle Rule, the company confirmed today.
The decision effectively ends new-car sales in the US for the Geely-owned Swedish EV brand — even though one of its models is assembled in South Carolina.

The Bureau of Industry and Security, part of the US Department of Commerce, declined to grant Polestar (Nasdaq: PSNY) an authorization to sell vehicles in the US from model year 2027 onward under the current Connected Vehicle Rule.

The rule, finalized in January 2025, bans connected vehicles with a “sufficient nexus” to China or Russia from the US market, with the software prohibitions taking effect for model year 2027 and hardware restrictions following in 2030. It covers telematics, cameras, microphones, GPS, Bluetooth, cellular modules, and automated driving software across gas, hybrid, and electric vehicles alike.

Polestar’s problem is ownership, not where the cars are built. The brand is majority-owned by Geely, the Chinese automotive group that also controls Volvo Cars. That nexus is what triggers the rule, regardless of the factory location — a dynamic that traces back to the Biden administration’s 2024 warning that Chinese-connected vehicles could harvest US driver data.

It’s a notable outcome given the geography of Polestar’s lineup. The Polestar 3 is built at Volvo’s plant in Charleston, South Carolina, while the Polestar 4 is assembled in Busan, South Korea — neither is made in China.
Here’s the catch: Volvo, also owned by Geely, was granted authorization to keep selling connected vehicles in the US.

H&M profit misses estimates as turnaround questions persist
sum: H&M AB reported disappointing sales, posing a fresh challenge to the Swedish fast-fashion retailer's turnaround efforts amid intense competition and cautious consumer spending.
Revenue in local currencies in the second quarter (2Q) fell 1%, compared with expectations for flat growth. H&M said sales in June are expected to be on par with the same month the previous year.

The company's shares, which slid as much as 5.2%, were trading 2.6% lower at 1.54pm in Stockholm. The stock had fallen about 9.3% this year through Wednesday's close. That compares with a decline of just under 1% in Zara owner Inditex's shares.

Chief executive officer Daniel Ervér's efforts to revive growth have come under increasing scrutiny after years of uneven performance. While investors have welcomed recent improvements in margins - supported by leaner inventory levels and stronger full-price sales - the focus has shifted to whether the retailer can restore consistent top-line growth. On a Thursday morning call, the CEO said the company's sales are "still not where we want them to be".
Hennes & Mauritz AB CEO Daniel Erver said in a Thursday morning call the company's sales are 'still not where we want them to be'.

"When looking at sales across the board, we are not satisfied," Ervér said. "We had plans for having stronger sales in this quarter," but even womenswear, where H&M had pushed for greater flexibility and better trend detection, was "affected by some supply gaps," he said.

While the company maintained its financial outlook for the year, it signalled signs of weak consumer sentiment in regions like Western Europe, a key market for H&M's womenswear. Although the weak dollar is providing some tailwinds, H&M said it expects higher transport costs, mainly related to elevated spot prices for airfreight and fuel surcharges.

Autonomous EV freight trucking company Einride rises sharply in first trade on Nasdaq
sum: Autonomous EV freight trucking company Einride rose sharply in its first day of trading on the Nasdaq. The company went public on Wednesday morning under the ticker symbol "ENRD."

Einride shares went higher by well over 100% during trading on Wednesday morning. Trading was temporarily halted by the Nasdaq mid-morning, based on its "limit up-limit-down" protocol that is triggered by rapid moves in the price of shares.

Einride's pre-equity value had fallen to $1.35 billion upon final shareholder approval of its SPAC deal with Legato Merger Corp. III last week — lower than the $1.8 billion value set when the deal was first proposed last November.
The deal raised over $200 million in gross proceeds, with $113 million in PIPE capital from institutional investors, including Stockholm-based EQT Ventures.

Founded in 2016, Einride provides heavy-duty, cab-less autonomous EV trucks, and freight services for driver-operated electric trucks. Its technology can also be licensed to third parties, both operational planning AI software and its autonomous driving system.
"In the majority of freight trucking uses cases in the future, electric and autonomous is going to be the cheapest options," said Einride CEO Roozbeh Charli in a "Squawk Box" interview on Wednesday.

Einride has 200 EV freight trucks operating on its platform today, "and doing so with a cost benefit today," Charli said. "You need to be cost efficient, and our customer deployments are already profitable today," he added.

sum: Volvo B stock (ISIN SE0000115446) represents the Swedish industrial group Volvo, which is active in heavy trucks, buses and construction equipment across global markets. As of September 6, 2026, investors are closely monitoring the company’s ability to translate demand in commercial vehicles and machinery into earnings growth and resilient cash flow. The shares remain a core vehicle for exposure to global freight, infrastructure and equipment cycles, with particular attention to cost discipline and margins.

Volvo Group’s latest reported figures, covering its most recent fiscal periods, show how the company has been navigating demand in trucks and construction equipment. In the latest available quarter within the freshness window up to mid-2026, Volvo reported multi-billion revenue in its industrial operations, underlining the scale of its heavy-vehicle franchise. A previous fiscal year comparison, used historically rather than as a current snapshot, showed revenue in the tens of billions of EUR-equivalent, illustrating the company’s long-term position in global commercial transport and infrastructure equipment.

Compared with an earlier fiscal year that is now only relevant as historical context, Volvo’s aggregated group revenue increased by a double-digit percent rate, with truck demand and construction equipment contributing the bulk of the growth. Historically, the group’s operating margin improved by several percentage points against that prior period, highlighting the impact of pricing measures, efficiency programs and a favorable product mix. These historical trends give investors a backdrop for assessing the current margin resilience, even though only the most recent interim and fiscal results within the allowed freshness window count as current for a same-day stock article.

In its most recently reported interim period within the nine-month freshness window, Volvo generated strong operating cash flow from its industrial business, reflecting solid conversion of earnings into liquidity. That cash flow supported investments in new truck platforms, electrification solutions and autonomous driving technologies, as well as dividend distributions and occasional share-repurchase programs as determined by the board.

Should Value Investors Buy Volvo (VLVLY) Stock?
sum: Here at Zacks, we focus on our proven ranking system, which places an emphasis on earnings estimates and estimate revisions, to find winning stocks. But we also understand that investors develop their own strategies, so we are constantly looking at the latest trends in value, growth, and momentum to find strong companies for our readers.

Of these, perhaps no stock market trend is more popular than value investing, which is a strategy that has proven to be successful in all sorts of market environments. Value investors use fundamental analysis and traditional valuation metrics to find stocks that they believe are being undervalued by the market at large.

In addition to the Zacks Rank, investors looking for stocks with specific traits can utilize our Style Scores system. Of course, value investors will be most interested in the system's "Value" category. Stocks with "A" grades for Value and high Zacks Ranks are among the best value stocks available at any given moment.

One stock to keep an eye on is Volvo (VLVLY). VLVLY is currently sporting a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), as well as an A grade for Value. The stock holds a P/E ratio of 11.98, while its industry has an average P/E of 19.35. Over the past year, VLVLY's Forward P/E has been as high as 13.87 and as low as 8.99, with a median of 11.52.

Another notable valuation metric for VLVLY is its P/B ratio of 3.45. The P/B ratio is used to compare a stock's market value with its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. This company's current P/B looks solid when compared to its industry's average P/B of 4.27. Over the past year, VLVLY's P/B has been as high as 3.71 and as low as 2.50, with a median of 3.04.

Value investors will likely look at more than just these metrics, but the above data helps show that Volvo is likely undervalued currently. And when considering the strength of its earnings outlook, VLVLY sticks out as one of the market's strongest value stocks.

ME Group shares tank on profit warning as Iran war hits revenues
sum: Shares in ME Group International tanked more than 26.5% on Monday after the self-service equipment company warned annual profits would be lower as the Iran war hit revenues at its photo-booth and laundry businesses in the first half of the fiscal year.
Group revenue in the six months to April 30 grew 2%, but the photobooth business was impacted by reduced demand for official photo ID amid ongoing travel uncertainty.
ME now expects FY 2026 profit before tax to be in the range of £69m to £74m, compared with £78.2m a year earlier.

“During April, the group experienced a softening in revenue, particularly in the French photobooth and laundry businesses. The board believes this is largely attributable to a shift in consumer spending patterns driven by lower consumer confidence due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East,” the company said in a trading update.
Wash.ME, the group's higher-margin business, was also impacted in April by a decline in consumer spending, with revenue in April up only 3% compared with an increase of 17% in H1 2026 overall.

“While there has been an improvement in trading through May, the board does not expect trading patterns to normalise while conflict in the Middle East and the subsequent uncertainty in the macroeconomic landscape continue.”

items.t: How a Berkshire Hathaway Company Helped Aurora Innovation Stock Soar Today
sum: Aurora Innovation (AUR +9.43%) stock took off today after the driverless vehicle technology company announced a new partnership with a Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary.

Aurora and Berkshire-owned McClane Company announced an arrangement to commence autonomous deliveries in Texas, utilizing an Aurora self-driving system initially being implemented in long-haul trucking. It expands on a prior pilot program, and it sent Aurora shares higher by 11% today, as of 12:45 p.m. ET.

Texas-based McClane serves convenience stores, large retailers, and restaurant chains and is an industry-leading partner to the biggest retail and restaurant businesses. The new agreement stems from a successful pilot program that transported 1,400 loads for McLane, helping serve restaurant clients throughout the state with a 100% on-time delivery rate.

Aurora intends to extend its operations to new routes connecting McLane distribution centers across the U.S. Sun Belt by the end of the year, with plans to accommodate more McLane business in the future.

Aurora has also just expanded an existing self-driving program with Volvo Group's Volvo Autonomous Solutions (V.A.S.), featuring a new 200-mile route connecting Dallas and Oklahoma City. Investors will likely hear more about both partnerships when Aurora reports first-quarter earnings after the bell today.

AUR Stock Eyes Fifth Straight Gain: Retail Bulls Cheer Aurora’s Volvo Deal
sum: Shares of Aurora Innovation, Inc. (AUR) are up in Tuesday’s premarket trading after the company and Volvo Autonomous Solutions announced they will establish a new 200-mile, five-day-a-week driverless trucking route between Dallas and Oklahoma City.

The deal follows the company’s Hirschbach agreement from last week, in which Aurora is helping the cold freight carrier achieve its goal of covering 500 million miles on longer, less desirable routes and deploy 500 trucks on the road by 2027.
At the time of writing, AUR shares were trading 1.5% higher, and if session gains hold throughout the day, the stock would record a five-day winning streak.
The new route between Dallas and Oklahoma City builds on the driverless truck tech company’s strategy to deploy its solutions in the U.S. Sun Belt, a high-volume trucking corridor.

Autonomous transportation is becoming increasingly popular in the U.S., as seen in the ongoing rise of “self-driving” robotaxis, and its use case for moving freight is growing, as it reduces operating costs and saves haulers time.

“Expanding our operations into Oklahoma City and adding customer endpoints is an important step for scaling autonomous transport,” said Sasko Cuklev, Head of On-Road Solutions at Volvo Autonomous Solutions.
Aurora, Volvo’s top autonomy partner, is among the first to deploy the Volvo VNL Autonomous across multiple U.S. states. The companies are now in the final validation phase for driverless operations.

items.t: Electric Trucks Market Size, Share & Trends Report 2026-2033, Competitive Analysis of Volvo, BYD, Daimler, Dongfeng, FAW, Foton, ISUZU, Navistar, PACCAR, and Scania
sum: Opportunities in the electric truck market include capitalizing on stricter emission regulations, leveraging expanding charging infrastructures, reduced battery costs, and governments' incentives. Increasing adoption by logistics operators and innovations enhancing truck performance also present significant growth potential.

Dublin, April 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The "Electric Trucks Market Size, Share & Trends Analysis Report by Vehicle Type (Light Duty Trucks, Medium Duty Trucks, Heavy Duty Trucks), Propulsion Type, Vehicle Range, Application, and Region with Growth Forecasts, 2026-2033" report has been added to ResearchAndMarkets.com's offering.
The global electric trucks market size was estimated at USD 39.30 billion in 2025, and is projected to reach USD 193.40 billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 20.9% from 2026 to 2033

This steady growth is attributed to stricter emission regulations, expanding charging infrastructure, falling battery costs, supportive government incentives, and increasing adoption of electric trucks by logistics and fleet operators to reduce operating costs and meet sustainability targets.

For instance, the Global EV Outlook 2023 report published by the International Energy Agency (IEA) revealed that over 60,000 medium- and heavy-duty electric trucks were sold worldwide in 2022, and a significant demand was observed from new markets. In addition, innovations in battery technology and economies of scale have led to significant reductions in battery costs, making electric trucks more competitive with their internal combustion (IC) engine counterparts. As the demand for environment-friendly logistics solutions increases, sales of electric trucks are expected to remain substantial over the forecast period.

A number of stringent emission standards and regulations have been implemented by governing bodies, such as the European Union's Euro 7, which is aimed at reducing pollution from vehicles, and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) Clean Trucks Plan that was announced in 2021 and will be applicable from 2027 onwards. These policies are compelling fleet operators to adopt cleaner alternatives in their operations, driving a higher demand for electric trucks.

sum: The Annual General Meeting adopted the income statement and balance sheet as well as the consolidated income statement and the consolidated balance sheet. items.t: VOLVO CE ANNOUNCES 2025 DEALER OF THE YEAR
sum: The award celebrates the dealership team that exemplifies the Volvo brand and consistently demonstrates high performance in service offerings, customer uptime and share performance.

In 2025, Power Equipment Company made an investment in the future with a new 52,000-square-foot headquarters in Brighton, Colorado, featuring 17 service bays and a dedicated training facility. They also implemented a centralized field service dispatch center to improve response times and minimize customer downtime.

“The Power Equipment Company team has committed to and invested in people and technology that ensure their customers get the right machine, right services and right advice every time,” said Scott Young, Head of Region North America, Volvo CE. “As a partner to Volvo CE, they're helping set the standard for how a dealership can drive long-term value through a customer-focused approach and deep-rooted expertise.”

That commitment translated into outstanding 2025 results, as Power Equipment Company achieved significant growth in machine sales and rental fleet capacity. The company is celebrating its 90th year in business and has partnered with Volvo CE for 40 years, supporting customers via seven locations across Colorado and New Mexico.

“This comes down to our people, plain and simple. We do not chase awards. We show up, do the work, and stand behind our customers when it counts,” said Mark Kuhn, Vice President of Construction Sales at Power Equipment Company. “This is the result of a team that is driven to deliver.”

sum: October 2026 Update: Volvo Unveils New VNX Heavy-Haul and Vocational Truck
Volvo Trucks North America highlighted new connectivity, safety tech and production investments at TMC. The OEM also signaled that a new heavy-haul flagship tractor is coming soon.
Volvo Trucks North America used its Technology & Maintenance Council (TMC) press conference to recap a sweeping, two-year product and investment cycle.
But tucked into the updates was a clear signal of what’s coming next: a new VNX model aimed at the heavy-haul segment, expected to debut later this year.

While much of the presentation revisited the rollout of Volvo’s new platform underpinning the recently launched VNL and VNR models, executives pointed to the upcoming VNX as the next major step in extending that architecture across the lineup.
“We’re in the midst of more than $2 billion in product investments,” said Magnus Koeck, vice president of strategy, marketing and brand management. “And we’re not done.”

Volvo stopped short of providing specifications or timing details. However, the confirmation of a next-generation VNX suggests the OEM is preparing to bring its new vehicle platform -- first introduced with the long-haul VNL-- into vocational and heavy-haul applications.

items.t: VW, Volvo and Mercedes recall over 100 thousand EVs. Batteries pose a fire risk
sum: Update of 24 October 2026: The original overview below covers January and February 2026. A new US NHTSA report 26V630 / Volkswagen 93EX dated 1 October lists 22 524 ID.4 vehicles from model years 2023–2026, built from 1 January 2023 to 1 February 2025. According to the report, the cause and final remedy are still being determined; until the repair, the manufacturer advises affected owners to charge to no more than 80%. We do not add this number to the earlier campaigns, and do not extrapolate the US scope to Czech cars. Volkswagen in the UK separately lists campaigns 93MV and 93MF for selected ID.3, ID.4 and ID.7 batteries from 2022 to 2025. The specific Czech vehicle must be checked against its VIN by an authorised service centre.

In the first two months of 2026, four major carmakers announced recalls covering more than 129 thousand electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids because of the risk of high-voltage battery fires. Volkswagen launched the largest campaign for the ID.4, followed by Volvo with the EX30 and Mercedes-Benz, which is recalling the EQB for the third time. The problem also affects the Ford Escape and Lincoln Corsair plug-in hybrids.
Volkswagen ID.4: over 52 thousand vehicles and two distinct problems

In January, Volkswagen announced two recall campaigns covering more than 52 thousand ID.4 electric vehicles in the US and Canada. The main campaign (NHTSA campaign 26V030) affects 43 881 vehicles from model years 2023 to 2025 that lack software to detect battery self-discharge (Self-Discharge Detection). Without this software, battery modules supplied by SK Battery America — the US subsidiary of South Korea's SK On — may overheat and catch fire.

The second campaign (26V028) covers around 670 vehicles from model years 2023 and 2024 with misaligned electrodes in their battery cells. This is the more serious fault: Volkswagen has ordered these vehicles to be parked outside immediately and not garaged after charging.
For both campaigns, Volkswagen is updating the software and will replace battery modules free of charge where necessary. Letters to owners were due to be sent by 20 March 2026.
In February, Mercedes-Benz announced its third recall campaign for almost 12 thousand EQB electric crossovers in the US.

Volvo B stock edges higher as hydrogen truck coalition lifts long term hopes
sum: AB Volvo B stock (ISIN SE0000115446) is trading modestly higher around 340.15 SEK on Cboe Europe as of September 3, 2026, up about 0.55% from the previous close of 338.30 SEK according to market data compiled by MarketScreener. The move comes on September 3, 2026, after the Swedish truck group announced it would join a broad industry coalition to accelerate hydrogen powered mobility in Europe.

On September 3, 2026, AB Volvo said it was teaming up with policymakers and major industrial partners in Germany and across Europe to build out a hydrogen mobility ecosystem for heavy transport, according to a company news release reported via MarketScreener. The coalition aims to scale hydrogen powered trucks and supporting infrastructure, positioning Volvo to benefit as regulators push for lower emissions in long haul transport.

The same report notes that the average target price for Volvo B shares stands at 353.28 SEK compared with the last close of 338.30 SEK as of September 3, 2026, implying an upside of about 4.43% based on analyst estimates collected by MarketScreener. This modest gap between price and target underlines that the stock is trading slightly below analysts' aggregate fair value view.

Real time quote data from MarketScreener show Volvo B at 340.15 SEK on Cboe Europe on September 3, 2026, with the share up 14.94% since the start of 2026 and down 1.82% over the most recent five day period. That combination of a double digit year to date gain and a small recent pullback suggests the stock has already priced in a fair portion of the companys fundamental progress while still reacting to short term news flow.

A parallel MarketScreener snapshot in euro terms indicates an indicative Volvo B price of 77.95 EUR with a market capitalization of about 71.47 billion SEK as of early trading on September 3, 2026, highlighting the companys status as one of the larger industrial names on the Stockholm exchange. For comparison, the same table shows other large European industrial and energy groups with market values between about 39 billion EUR and 234 billion JPY equivalent, placing Volvo in the upper mid range of the regional heavy industry universe.

Mack® Keystone® Makes World Debut at ConExpo-Con/Agg 2026
sum: “The Mack Keystone represents our commitment to providing customers in agriculture, construction and vocational markets with a truck that’s as capable on rough terrain as it is on the highway,” said Stephen Roy, president of Mack Trucks. “Named after the Keystone State of Pennsylvania, where all Mack Class 8 models for North America and export are assembled at Lehigh Valley Operations in Macungie, the Keystone continues Mack’s tradition of building rugged, reliable trucks that work as hard as the people who drive them.”

The Keystone builds on the strong legacy of the Mack Pinnacle™, which has earned a reputation for durability and high customer satisfaction over its 20+ years in Mack’s product lineup. The Keystone delivers all the same advanced technology and safety as the Mack Pioneer™ and all-new Mack Anthem®—along with the new Mack Granite®, also unveiled at ConExpo-Con/Agg 2026. This unified platform enables the Keystone model to offer identical comfort features, safety systems and performance technologies while maintaining the heavy-duty characteristics essential for vocational tractor applications.

“Our customers told us they wanted a truck that could handle the toughest jobs and job sites without compromising driver comfort or modern technology,” said Jonathan Randall, president of Mack Trucks North America.
“The Keystone delivers exactly that: terrain versatility to navigate challenging road conditions, combined with the best ride quality in the business.”

The Keystone is engineered for customers who operate in construction, agriculture, logging, livestock hauling and other applications that require a truck capable of performing on highways and challenging off-road terrain. Key to this capability is the Keystone’s higher ground clearance, approach angle and robust suspension system. The available Mack Maxride™ suspension is specifically engineered to deliver ultimate performance on the most demanding road conditions, providing best-in-class ride quality whether on highway or rough terrain.
